After closing, expectations for desk cover
This page walks new staff through what to do first

This page is about after-closing desk cover at the Companion Animal Travel Desk, and it matters because the last handoff of the day keeps travelers, handlers, and the next shift from starting from behind. When the front counter quiets down, your job is not to rush out; it is to make the desk steady, tidy, and ready for the next round of animal travel support. Start by checking the active file tray, the inbound notes, and any messages left by the welcome team so nothing is missed. If a carrier has moved through the day, confirm that the record matches the current status and that the ground team has noted any change in condition or location.

Keep your tone calm and your steps measured. Animals do better when the people around them stay gentle and predictable, so do not crowd a carrier or add extra handling without a clear reason. If a traveler needs help with a pet already in the care flow, bring the issue to the senior coordinator in plain language and follow the usual stepwise review. That means you gather the facts, check what has already been done, and then hand off the concern in a way that does not create confusion for the next person.

Desk cover also means protecting clean surfaces, locking away sensitive papers, and leaving visible notes where the next staff member will actually see them. Update the handoff sheet with what is finished, what is pending, and what still needs a human eye. If something feels off, do not guess. Call it out early, because small gaps become bigger problems when they are left for the morning team.

The best end-of-day work is calm, complete, and easy to pick up. Remember to leave the Companion Animal Travel Desk ready, accurate, and reassuring for whoever comes next.
